Overall objective: Improved sector capacity to implement environmentally sound waste management policies.
0a: Waste infrastructure investment plans integrated by the national government in the infrastructure programs in other provinces 0b: Waste infrastructure investment plans integrated by the national government in the infrastructure programs in other provinces 0c: Number of settlements with raised capacity for waste sorting at source (separate waste collection coverage in the country) 0d: Number of targeted businesses having intention to invest or expand investment in the WM sector.
Outcome 1: EPR (Extended Producer's Responsibility) system developed
Outcome 2: National technical guidance for Waste source separation applied in the pilot municipality
Outcome 3: Capacities built for achieving Outcome 1 and Outcome 2, as well as for scaling up the achieved results

Förstärkt genomförande av Armeniens avfallspolicy genom: 1) Framstagande av regelverk för införande av producentansvar, kapacitetsbyggande samt inköp av dataprogram för hantering av avfallsinformation, samt 2) framtagande av nationell model för källsortering (hushållsnivå), genomförande av pilotinsats i en kommun, inklusive kapacitietsbyggande, informationskampanj och utrustning (en sopbil och avfallskärl).

Strengthened implementation of Armenia's waste management policy through 1) Development of legal framework for an Extended Producer Responsibility, capacity building and purchase of data management system IT) and 2) development of a national model for household source separation, implementation of a pilot project on source separation in one Municipality, including capacity building, information and awareness campaign and purchase of one refuse vehicle and waste bins.

Summary of progress reported for August 2024 to August 2025
The WPA (Waste Policy Armenia) programme has made notable progress during the past year. Reported progress statements and indicators have so far primarily been linked linked to regulatory frameworks and policy developments supported by the programme, and to the design, resourcing and implementation of municipal pilot operations for improved waste management practices in Sevan municipality.
With regards to implementation of improved waste management practices in the Sevan municipality, delays revealed unexpected challenges and lessons related to procurement. Procurement of equipment for the Sevan pilot was a major milestone of the year, and required a much larger effort than expected at all levels. The formal launch of upgraded operations in Sevan was held in July 26, 2025 and received a lot of attention in Armenia.
Otherwise, most activities continued quite successfully according to plan, with an activity implementation rate for the first half of current activity year at 94%. At outcome level the achievement rate was relatively slower at 50%
A major independent stocktaking of programme progress was submitted with the Mid-term Review (MTR) in February 2025. Its overall conclusions were encouraging with the following key observations;
- The program interventions are highly relevant to the country context and strategic national plans in the field. - Despite challenges and delays, the program has effectively engaged in addressing key issues within the waste management system and is likely to achieve most of the planned outcomes. - The programs implementation efficiency has room for improvement through enhanced planning, better resource utilization, and further streamlining of its M&E system. - Sustainability of program outcomes requires further attention due to heavy reliance on the program team, limited ministry capacity and ownership for EPR implementation, financial and operational capacity constraints of businesses, and limited public preparedness. - The program demonstrates strong integration of cross-cutting issues through comprehensive gender mainstreaming, human rights approaches, and environmental considerations.
In addition to reported progress towards national waste policy upgrading, which is now pending formal approval, and municipal waste system reform as reported for the municipality of Sevan, private sector engagement in the sector is a third central pillar of local waste management reform. Progress has been slow in this objective area, but results began to materialize in 2025. In a status assessment and support intervention carried out by Sida's helpdesk, the programme has struggled to find solid ground on private sector engagement but demonstrated improvements in 2025 and good opportunities to catch up on sustainable market development during the remaining and final year of the programme. The assessment report underscores several key observations and recommendations from the MTR and highlights, among other things, the following effects linked to programme engagements;
- There are promising signs of sustainability in core markets, but that the program is now challenged to retrofit considerations of sustainability to supporting markets in the last year of implementation - The program has sought to address underlying reasons for under-performance in the policy process with the result that the underlying policy process has been strengthened. New practices have been adopted by stakeholders in the policy ecosystem. (New practices are detailed in the report.) - AUA's provision of direct support in sub-markets relevant to EPR legislation, has delivered result. The challenge in the last year of implementation is for these behaviors to be sustained, in EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) and other waste systems. - The government, the private sector and media companies are more aware of the benefits of receiving technical assistance, and of the importance of relationships. There is expertise within Armenia, and internationally, and AUA has demonstrated its ability to enable relationships between stakeholders. - The government is showing increasing ownership of the EPR policy and legislation. - Advocacy is now more possible because of support to the program supported Producer Responsibility Organisation (PRO) and the Recyclers Union. Further, the PRO will demonstrate the value of EPR systems. - Support to the establishment of PRO involves piloting of new practices contained in the EPR legislation, on a voluntary basis. It demonstrates progress towards systemic change within the narrowly defined system of bottlers in pilot municipalities, and progress towards broader system wide change in systems where EPR has relevance. - The American Chamber of Commerce Armenia has also supported the PRO. This support has included the establishment of Sustainable Waste Management Committee, and engaging its members for financial commitment. This support has resulted in a number of new behaviors among market system actors. - The program's support to the Armenian Union of Recyclers represents progress towards addressing underlying constraints to the design and implementation of effective regulations for recycling. One enacted, these regulations will stimulate new practices, through increased innovation and investment, in recycling. - A range of new practices emanating from these efforts are detailed in the report.
During 2025, a challenge fund trial operation has also reached the stage of implementation. It seeks to stimulate better private sector practices related to waste management. Selecting a format for this pilot operation has been time-consuming and the launch has been delayed throughout 2024. In the summer of 2025, AUA has entered collaboration with a procured challenge fund partner, Impact Hub, and the fund is now launched. It is designed to address perceived risks of investment and innovation in new practices, which are in turn expected to create wide scale and sustainable changes in waste management systems over time. The assumption is that the risks are perceived, not realized, and that financial institutions or businesses would not invest in solutions with good potential of systemic impact. While the fund itself is not intended to be a permanent facility in the markets, the innovations and investment practices that it seeks to catalyze are expected to be sustained beyond the fund itself.
Finally there was also progress noted in the area of biogas production developments during 2025. The biogas workstream is an originally unexpected result for the programme, which was added adaptively in response to increased public and private sector demands identified during 2024. With the completion of a large national feasibility study for biogas production completed in dialogue with relevant authorities during Q1 2025, a stakeholder consultation and roadmap drafting exercise was also completed (in May 2025).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
